فُلَاقٌ : see فِلْقَةٌ, in two places. ―
-b2- Also, (O, K,) and فُلُوقٌ, (thus in the O,) or ↓ فَلُوقٌ , like صَبُورٌ, (thus in the K, [but this I think questionable,]) Milk becoming, or become, like cheese: (O, K:) [or فُلَاقٌ may be here a quasi-pl. n. of فِلْقٌ (q. v. voce فِلْقَةٌ), so that the meaning may be, that has become cleft portions of curd; and فُلُوقٌ may also mean thus as a pl. of فِلْقٌ. See also the next paragraph.]
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
